Subject: Re: Fw: Request: 99.99% availability + sub-60ms p95 for production rollout

Vanessa / Marissa —

Quick technical read: 50ms p95 is aggressive but potentially achievable under the following conditions:
- Model must be a quantized LLM (8-bit/4-bit) or a small-medium transformer (<=7B) with KV cache warming.
- Dedicated low-latency pools (pinned instances) with prewarmed KV cache and continuous batching disabled for hot routes.
- Canary routing & warm standby across two AZs in us-west to avoid single-AZ blips.

We can't promise 50ms at all sequence lengths. For seq <=100 tokens and trimmed input it's plausible. Also need to accept carveouts during major kernel upgrades or noisy-neighbor incidents — that should be defined in an exception clause.

Ops items: we'll need guaranteed reserved GPUs (we can propose a priority capacity pool), a runbook that includes automatic fallback to a compatible latency-optimized variant (same model family, aggressive quantization), and a burst credit system to cover sustained peak > baseline.

I'll draft a technical appendix with measurable constraints. If Marissa can weigh in on contractual precedent/discount range, we can bundle into an approval note for Grace.

Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime

Team —

Commercial frame: customer will need to accept a carveout schedule and an operational credit policy. For a committed 12m reserved capacity deal we can consider a 10-20% discount off list, but premium SLAs require a fee add-on (SLA guardrail surcharge) and an accelerated incident response SLA (SRE rotation on-call with 30 min escalation).

I recommend the following approval path:
1) Technical appendix from Karthik outlining exact measurable p95 test cases and exception windows.
2) Ops runbook & capacity design from SRE (two-AZ standby, priority pool).
3) Legal to draft a tailored SOW with carveouts for maintenance, major code/infra upgrades, and force majeure.
4) Grace (Exec) to signoff on the commercial uplift and exception authority.

I'll prepare a short commercial memo. If we can get product + infra signoff by 12/3 EOD, I'll circulate the SOW stub to StratNet.

-Marissa
Head of Commercial Operations

Thanks for the clear path. Two operational notes before I sign:
- We should avoid absolute language in marketing/contract. Put the p95 commitment behind measurable traffic shapes and a qualified model list. (E.g., "for supported model tiers and request profiles specified in Appendix A").
- Approve a 99.99% monthly uptime threshold only if the customer accepts 2 operational concessions: 1) mandatory 2-AZ warm standby and 2) a quarterly joint runbook review.

I'm OK to approve the commercial uplift (add-on + 12m reserved) if Legal signs off on the exception language and SRE confirms capacity can be reserved without disrupting our other top-accounts.

Grace O'Connor
VP, Commercial Strategy

Anya —

Appreciate the patience while we reviewed internally. Short summary and next steps (we've attached the draft commitment language and ops diff):

What we can offer
- A tailored SOW that commits to 99.99% monthly uptime for the StratNet production routes, scoped to the model tiers and traffic profiles in Appendix A.
- A target p95 of 50ms for trimmed requests within the supported model list (seq <=100 tokens). This will be delivered from a Dedicated priority pool in us-west with two-AZ warm standby and prewarmed KV caches.

Guardrails & carveouts
- Carveouts apply for scheduled maintenance, major runtime upgrades, and force majeure. We will include a defined exception window (max 4 hours per major kernel upgrade) and an incident credit schedule.
- If you exceed agreed steady-state QPS for >24 hours, we will shift to negotiated burst pricing or activate the fallback variant (latency-optimized).

Commercials
- 12-month reserved capacity commitment with SLA surcharge (commercial memo attached). Pricing will be final once Legal confirms SOW language.

Next steps
1) Karthik to deliver the technical appendix (ETA: 12/03 EOD).
2) SRE/ops runbook and capacity reservation to be confirmed (attachment: ops-runbook-diff.txt).
3) Legal to review draft SOW; Marissa will share commercial memo.

We're prepared to include a short "shadow decision log" in the SOW appendix that documents the operational exceptions and the escalation path for any approved carveouts. That will make audit reviews simpler on your side.

Can you confirm you want us to proceed to SOW draft?

Best,
Vanessa
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
